{{Current events|year=2018|month=04|day=28|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[2018 Gaza border protests]]
**[[Israel]] launches airstrikes on [[Hamas]] ships in [[Gaza City|Gaza]]'s port and a Hamas building in [[Deir al-Balah]] in response to the ongoing, and sometimes violent, protests. [https://www.ynetnews.com/articles/0,7340,L-5244233,00.html (Ynetnews)]
**Protestor Azzam Aweida, 15, dies of injuries sustained when the [[Israeli Defence Forces]] shot him yesterday. [https://nypost.com/2018/04/28/palestinian-teen-protesting-on-gaza-border-killed-by-israeli-fire/ (''The New York Post'')]
**[[Egypt]] opens the [[Rafah Crossing]] into the [[Gaza Strip]] for three days, saying it is to be used by students, those requiring medical assistance, and people with permits to enter Egypt. [https://www.haaretz.com/middle-east-news/palestinians/egypt-opens-gaza-s-rafah-crossing-for-three-days-1.6033525 (Haaretz)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)]]
**A car bomb targeting a [[Afghan National Army|military base]] in the Nadali District of [[Helmand]], [[Afghanistan]], kills six including two soldiers. [https://edition.cnn.com/2018/04/28/asia/afghanistan-bombing-helmand-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*A [[suicide bomb]]ing in a restaurant in [[Galkayo]], [[Somalia]], kills three military officials and two soldiers. Eight more people are injured, some critically. [[al-Shabaab (militant group)|al-Shabaab]] claims responsibility. [https://edition.cnn.com/2018/04/28/africa/somalia-bomb-attack-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Hamas]] accuses the [[Palestinian Authority]] of performing a bombing [[false flag|against its own]] Prime Minister, [[Rami Hamdallah]]. Hamdallah escaped injury when his convoy was bombed during a visit to the Hamas-controlled [[Gaza Strip]] last month. [http://www.middleeasteye.net/news/hamas-accuses-pa-over-bomb-attempt-its-own-premier-1419603310 (Middle East Eye)]
;Arts and culture
*[[Art forgery]]
**82 paintings at a museum dedicated to [[Étienne Terrus]] in [[Elne]], [[France]], are revealed as forgeries. [http://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-43933530 (BBC)]
*Cardinal [[Angelo Amato]], acting on behalf of [[Pope Francis]], beatifies [[Hanna Chrzanowska]] in [[Kraków]], [[Poland]]. Chrzanowska dedicated her life to helping the sick and homeless and had worked with Cardinal [[Karol Wojtyła]], who led her funeral services before he became [[Pope John Paul II]]. [http://www.thenews.pl/1/9/Artykul/361021,Polish-nurse-beatified (Radio Poland)]
*Bone remains of more than 140 children and about 200 young llamas were found in the Peruvian city of [[Trujillo, Peru|Trujillo]], near the [[Chan Chan]] citadel, according to a [[National Geographic]] publication. This discovery, which would date from the time of the little-known [[Chimú culture|Chimú]] pre-Columbian civilization (about 550 years ago), would be, for researchers, the largest mass sacrifice of children in the American continent. [https://elcomercio.pe/peru/la-libertad/precedentes-america-lugar-masivo-sacrificio-ninos-antiguo-peru-noticia-515313?foto=1 (''El Comercio'')] [https://www.nationalgeographic.co.uk/video/tv/history-101-chimu (''National Geographic'')]
*A statue honouring [[comfort women]], sex slaves raped by [[Japan]]ese [[World War II]] soldiers, in [[Manila]], [[Philippines]], is removed less than five months after it was installed. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2018-04/28/c_137144177.htm (Xinhua)]
;Disasters and accidents
*A communal toilet collapses in [[Bhandup]], [[Mumbai]], [[India]]. Several people are trapped and require rescue, with two dying ''en route'' to hospital. [https://www.firstpost.com/india/two-dead-in-mumbais-bhandup-after-wall-roof-of-community-toilet-collapse-probe-underway-4449247.html (''First Post'')]
;International relations
*[[Sanctions against North Korea]]
**[[Australia]] and [[Canada]] deploy surveillance aircraft to [[Japan]] to monitor ship-to-ship transfers between [[North Korea]]n vessels that bypass [[United Nations]] sanctions. The aircraft join a warship already deployed by the [[United Kingdom]]. [http://www.cbc.ca/news/world/north-korea-un-sanctions-surveillance-1.4640082 (CBC)]
*[[Panmunjom Declaration]], [[South Korea–United States relations]]
**[[United States Defense Secretary]] [[James Mattis]] and [[Ministry of National Defense (South Korea)|South Korea Defense Minister]] [[Song Young-moo]] say they are committed to "a diplomatic resolution that achieves complete, verifiable and irreversible denuclearization" of [[North Korea]], according to a [[The Pentagon|Pentagon]] spokesperson. Mattis repeats the United States' "ironclad" commitment to defend its ally [[South Korea]] "using the [[Full-spectrum dominance|full spectrum]] of U.S. capabilities." [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/mattis-reaffirms-ironclad-u-s-commitment-to-defending-south-korea-2018-04-28/ (CBS News)]
;Law and crime
*A judge in the U.S. state of [[Oklahoma]] dismisses charges against seven detainees over a prison riot that killed four at [[Cimarron Correctional Facility]] in 2015. [http://www.stwnewspress.com/news/charges-dismissed-in-fatal-prison-riot/article_67182bbd-f170-572b-80a5-62a82123fc48.html (Stillwater News Press)]
*[[Worthing]] [[Magistrates Court]] fines the [[Church of Scientology]] [[pound sterling|£]]14,000 and orders it to pay £2,566 in costs for polluting the [[River Medway]] in [[West Sussex]], [[England]], with raw sewage. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/scientology-sewage-leak-fined-sussex-church-pollution-river-medway-a8326821.html (The Independent)]
*[[Terrorism in Iran]]
**An [[Iran]]ian [[Revolutionary Court]] begins a trial of eight alleged [[ISIL|Islamic State]] members accused of involvement in gun and [[suicide bomb]] attacks that killed eighteen in [[Tehran]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-iran-security-trial/trial-begins-in-iran-over-deadly-attacks-claimed-by-islamic-state-idUSKBN1HZ0H5 (Reuters)]
